description: Ground truth for tests/Fixtures/GroundTruth/CallShapes. The list is complete: it holds every fact of a compared kind whose source and target are both declared in the fixture. GroundTruthGoldenTests compares the extractor output in that scope with this list as an exact set, in both directions. Each fact names its basis: the evidence that makes the fact true without the extractor (see basis_values). A fact with 'pending' is true, but the extractor does not write it yet; the test requires it to be absent until the named stage removes the 'pending' field. Other kinds (Returns, Throws, Declares, Inherits, Implements, Overrides, Hides, MayDispatchTo, StaticallyCalls, ExtensionReceiver, Contains, the Reflection kinds and the adapter kinds) are not compared here; GoldenEdgeTests, GoldenReflectionTests and GoldenAdapterTests cover them.
symbol_id_format: Facts carry the Roslyn documentation-comment id only. The snapshot id is 'docCommentId|assemblyDisplayName' (SymbolIdFactory.Make); append the assembly from the projects list, or resolve the doc id against the snapshot. Doc ids are unique across the two projects in this fixture.

basis_values.symbolfinder: Roslyn SymbolFinder.FindReferencesAsync reports a reference to the target inside the source member (for Calls, also FindCallersAsync), and the syntax at that reference gives the kind.
basis_values.language-rule: Roslyn reports no reference location (an implicit call or read, or a type inside a function-pointer type). The fact follows from the C# language rule that the reason names, derived by hand.
basis_values.convention:D8: Owner rule: the member that runs the code owns the fact (mapping rule 5). Roslyn names a different owner here.
basis_values.convention:D10: using target rule (mapping rule 9). SymbolFinder reports a using as a reference to every Dispose implementation, so it is no evidence for the target.
basis_values.convention:D38: A compiler-made member that Lurp stores gets the signature facts of a written member (mapping rule 6). Roslyn reports no location because the member has no syntax.
basis_values.convention:D126: A compiler-made member's return type is a signature References fact, like the return type of a written member (mapping rule 6).
basis_values.convention:D12: D12 rule: a member depends on the inferred type of a local or of an implicitly typed lambda parameter like on a written type (mapping rule 7). Roslyn reports no location because the source names no type.
basis_values.convention:D136: D136 rule: a lambda or anonymous method depends on its return type, written or inferred (mapping rule 7). Roslyn reports no location because the source names no type.

mapping: 1. Calls: an invocation in a body is a Calls fact to the bound method. This includes the implicit calls of the C# rules: foreach (GetEnumerator, MoveNext; Current is a read), using (rule 9), await (GetAwaiter, GetResult; IsCompleted is a read), deconstruction and positional patterns (Deconstruct), a collection initializer (Add), a collection expression of a type with Add (Add for each element), a spread element (GetEnumerator, MoveNext; Current is a read), a collection builder (the builder method), list patterns and implicit index and range (Count or Length is a read, the int indexer is a read, Slice is a call), user-defined operators and conversions, an interpolated-string handler (its constructor and the Append calls) and 'with' (the record clone method). A recursive call is a Calls fact from the member to itself.

2. Constructs: an object creation (also target-typed new()), an attribute application and an interpolated-string handler creation are Constructs facts to the created type. Each is also a Calls fact to the bound constructor when that constructor is declared in source; an implicitly declared constructor gets no Calls fact. A constructor initializer (this(...) or base(...)) and the arguments of a primary-constructor base list are Calls facts to the constructor.
3. MethodGroupRef: a method group that converts to a delegate is a MethodGroupRef fact. The handler of an event += and of an event -= is such a conversion.

4. Reads and Writes: '=', an out argument and a deconstruction or tuple target are writes. A compound assignment, ??=, ++, --, a ref argument and a ref local or ref return alias are a read and a write. Every other use (also an in argument) is a read. An event: += and -= are writes; every other use (for example a raise) is a read. An indexer access reads or writes the indexer property.

5. Owner (the source of a fact): the member that runs the code. An accessor body (also an expression-bodied property or indexer) is owned by the accessor method. A field or property initializer is owned by the field or property. The arguments of a primary-constructor base list are owned by the primary constructor. A local function, a lambda and a query clause are owned by the member that contains them. A parameter default value is owned by the method (an indexer parameter: the indexer property; a delegate parameter: the delegate type). An enum member value is owned by the enum member. A field-like event initializer is owned by the event. An attribute argument is owned by the attributed member (a type attribute: the type; a parameter or return-value attribute: its method).

6. References from signatures: each source type named in a member signature (the return type, the parameter types, the type of a property, field or event, with their type arguments, array elements and function-pointer types) is a References fact from that member. A delegate type owns its own signature. An accessor and an enum member add no signature fact of their own. A compiler-made member that Lurp stores gets the same signature facts as a written member. A type argument in a base list and each type in a generic constraint are References facts from the declaring type (a method constraint: from the method).

7. References from bodies: each source type named in a body is a References fact from the owner. This includes the receiver type of a static member access (an invocation, a method group, a field, a property, an event or a constant), a local declaration (written or inferred type, also an implicitly typed lambda parameter), the return type of a lambda or anonymous method (written or inferred), is and type patterns, casts, default(T), sizeof, array creation, catch types and method type arguments. An object creation gives a Constructs fact, not a References fact. typeof gives ReflectionTypeRef, which this list does not compare.

8. C# 14 extension blocks: a call to a block method targets the implementation method on the outer static class. A read or write of a block property targets the block property. The receiver type of the block is a References fact from each implementation member.

9. using and await using: the target is the member that implements IDisposable.Dispose (IAsyncDisposable.DisposeAsync) on the static type of the resource. A ref struct uses its own Dispose pattern method. For a type parameter, its effective base class decides. A nullable value type uses its underlying type. When the target is an interface method outside the fixture, or the resource is dynamic, there is no fact.

notes.reason: FromDynamic binds a dynamic receiver; a dynamic invocation has no statically resolved symbol, so it must surface as binding incompleteness rather than an edge. The CoreApi.DynamicTarget() call in the same body is a normal Calls fact.

'original with { Id = ... }' calls the record clone method M:CallShapes.Core.ShapeRecord.{Clone}$, then the init setter (Writes P:CallShapes.Core.ShapeRecord.Id). The clone call is a Calls fact (mapping rule 1).

FromCollectionExpression returns [1, 2, 3]. Array types have no persisted symbol (no T:System.Int32[] row in the snapshot), so the array construction cannot be a persistable edge target; the construct is present for crash/incompleteness coverage.
C# requires attribute constructor arguments to be compile-time constants, so the only extractable fact in [ShapeMarker(19)] is the construction of ShapeMarkerAttribute.

C# requires default parameter values to be compile-time constants, so no call can occur in one. The fixture exercises the omitted-argument call shape instead (FromOmittedArgument calls OmittedArgumentTarget without passing its constant default).

NestedDerived.Value overrides NestedBase.Value. The Overrides edge is outside this oracle's kinds; the B20 self-index check in Part D step 3 covers Overrides, Declares, Returns and Throws from nested types.

A call to a C# 14 block method binds to a compiler-made nested symbol (M:CallShapes.Core.ShapeTextExtensions.<G>$0A9D361FAFE148655B241EBC2970963E.BlockWordCount). Roslyn's AssociatedExtensionImplementation maps it to M:CallShapes.Core.ShapeTextExtensions.BlockWordCount(CallShapes.Core.ShapeText), the fact target. A block property has no implementation symbol, so its reads and writes target the block property (P:...<G>$....BlockTag). Accessor bodies are owned by the implementation accessor.

ShapeUsingCallers holds one using for each target branch of mapping rule 9. FromInterfaceUsing and FromInterfaceConstrainedUsing target System.IDisposable.Dispose, and FromDynamicUsing has no static target, so these three members have no using fact.
